properties.areaDesc: South Slopes Of The Central Brooks Range
properties.headline: Winter Storm Watch issued October 28 at 3:58PM AKDT until October 31 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow possible. Total snow accumulations between 6 and
12 inches possible.

* WHERE...South Slopes Of The Central Brooks Range.

* WHEN...From Thursday evening through Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Temperatures Friday and Saturday afternoons
will hover around freezing. Under heavy snowfall rates,
precipitation will remain all snow. However, if there are breaks in
the heavy snow, warmer air may try to intrude resulting in areas of
drizzle of light rain. If there are wet spots, these will freeze as
temperatures drop into the 20s each night.
properties.instruction: Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

properties.description:

one inch.

* WHERE...In Oregon, North Oregon Cascades. In Washington, South
Washington Cascades.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely
become slick and hazardous.

non-perishable food items, tire chains, etc.

visit: wsdot.com/travel/real-time/map

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 28 at 7:54PM EDT until October 29 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday
evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 PM EDT
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Ashland, WI; Bayfield, WI; Sawyer, WI
properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 28 at 6:53PM CDT until October 28 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Duluth MN
properties.description:
SVRDLH

The National Weather Service in Duluth MN has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southeastern Bayfield County in northwestern Wisconsin...
Southwestern Ashland County in northwestern Wisconsin...
North central Sawyer County in northwestern Wisconsin...

* Until 800 PM CDT.

* At 653 PM CDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from Drummond to Cable to near Seeley, moving northeast
at 50 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Severe thunderstorms will be near...
Namekagon Lake around 700 PM CDT.
Namekagon around 705 PM CDT.
Sanborn around 710 PM CDT.

Other locations in the path of these severe thunderstorms include
Marengo, Mellen and Copper Falls State Park.
properties.instruction:
A Tornado Watch remains in effect until 900 PM CDT for northwestern
Wisconsin.

Remain alert for a possible tornado! Tornadoes can develop quickly
from severe thunderstorms. If you spot a tornado, go at once into the
basement or small central room in a sturdy structure.

For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.areaDesc: Hudspeth, TX
properties.senderName: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 28 at 5:48PM MDT until October 28 at 8:45PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Hudspeth County in western Texas...

* WHEN...Until 845 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 548 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Up to 1.25 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall of up to 0.5 inches is expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Dell City and Salt Flat.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 845 PM MDT THIS EVENING

properties.areaDesc: South Slopes of the Western Brooks Range; Noatak Valley
properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 28 at 3:47PM AKDT until October 29 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 6 and
12 inches near Red Dog Mine and 12 to 18 inches in the Western
Brooks Range. Winds gusting as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Red Dog Mine and the South Slopes of the Western Brooks
Range.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Mostly rain is expected below 800 feet,
including Noatak. The heaviest snow is expected Wednesday afternoon
into Thursday morning. Temperatures cool through tonight and into
Thursday.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency.

NWSheadline: WINTER STORM WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 4 PM AKDT THURSDAY

properties.areaDesc: Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Interior Seward Peninsula
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 28 at 3:46PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
ESFAFG

Areas of concern are between Nome and Council, particularity streams
and rivers draining the south aspects of the high elevation terrain
of the Seward Peninsula.

Rivers and streams in the Nome and Council area are already high
following rainfall over the weekend and early this week. Around 0.25
to 0.50" of additional rain is expected by the end of the week which
will keep water levels high. No flooding is expected but those along
the rivers and streams should be vigilant of the high water that is
expected through the end of the week.

NWSheadline: HYDROLOGIC OUTLOOK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH FRIDAY MORNING FOR THE SEWARD PENINSULA

properties.areaDesc: Otero, NM
properties.senderName: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 28 at 5:44PM MDT until October 28 at 7:45PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Otero County in south central New Mexico...

* Until 745 PM MDT.

* At 544 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of North Central Otero County.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: Lincoln, NM
properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 28 at 5:42PM MDT until October 28 at 6:15PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 542 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 9 miles south of
Hondo, or 20 miles east of Ruidoso. This storm was stationary.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and half dollar size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly rural areas of Southeastern Lincoln County.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

Heavy rains from severe thunderstorms can produce sudden and
dangerous flows in arroyos, ditches and over low water crossings. Do
not attempt to drive through areas where water covers the roadway.

NWSheadline: SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 615 PM MDT FOR SOUTHEASTERN LINCOLN COUNTY

properties.areaDesc: Wabasha; Buffalo
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 28 at 6:40PM CDT by NWS La Crosse WI
properties.description:
At 639 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Wabasha, moving northeast at 50 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 45 mph and penny to dime size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

This strong thunderstorm will be near...
Wabasha and Alma around 645 PM CDT.
Modena around 650 PM CDT.

Other locations impacted by this storm include Gilmanton, Nelson,
Pioneer Campground, Zumbro Bottoms Campground, Conception, Misha
Mokwa, County Roads F And K K, Lock And Dam 4, The Big Swamp Area,
and Dumfries.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead
to localized flooding in areas of poor drainage. Do not drive your
vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.areaDesc: East Carteret
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 28 at 7:35PM EDT until October 29 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1 to 2 feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...East Carteret County.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Thursday
evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM EDT
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level
is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways resulting in a low threat of property damage. Some
roads and low lying property including parking lots, parks,
lawns, and homes adjacent to the waterfront will experience
shallow flooding. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels will remain high with a King
Tide Cycle in place through Thursday. The morning high tide
will be the highest of the two daily tides.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
